html:
One Script, End to End

ServiceRelationWhat happens
1Release deskdesk:releaseA person asks; the desk starts ARTIE on the kept script
2Gatewayscm:pulls-getOpen the pull request
3Offer watchwatcher:watchTell me when it offers scm:merge; wait for the reply
4Gatewayscm:mergeMerge by squashing; check it’s merged
5CI · Jenkinsci:buildBuild the merge commit; wait for the reply
6CI · Jenkinsci:smoke-testRun the build’s own smoke scenarios against its deployment
7Dev, or the gatewayenv:promote or scm:commentAll passed: promote. One failed: say why on the pull request

Five services, one script written as data, one generic client.
say: Here's the whole release on one slide. A person asks the release desk to release a pull request: desk:release. The desk starts ARTIE on the kept script. ARTIE opens the pull request through the gateway, scm:pulls-get. It asks the watcher to say when merge is offered, and waits. Answered: it merges, scm:merge, by squashing, and checks the pull request really is merged. It asks CI to build the merge commit, ci:build, and waits. Answered: it follows the link to the build, and runs the smoke scenarios the build links, against the deployment the build links. If they all pass, it opens Dev and promotes the commit, env:promote, citing how many passed. If one fails, it doesn't promote; it says why on the pull request, scm:comment. Five services. One script, written as data. One generic client. And every step is a control the last answer offered.
